title: Observability ingest replay checklist and quick experiments
content:
TL;DR:
Quick scratchpad for reproducing and debugging the recent drop in tracing/log ingestion (2024-10-14 incident). Focus: replaying batches into the ingest gateway, isolating OTLP export failures, and checking hook registration timing. This is messy — notes to self.

Incident summary (short):
- Around 2024-10-14 22:30 UTC we saw a ~30% drop in spans and ~45% drop in logs_ingested_total for ~18m.
- Affected services: inference-proxy (ingress), obs-ingester (k8s), otel-collector (sidecar + central).
- Symptoms: metrics drop, traces show long queueing in otel exporter, and the ingester reported intermittent 429 from downstream storage.

Observed evidence / quick artifacts to check:
- PromQL to surface drop: sum(rate(logs_ingested_total[5m])) by (cluster)  
- Spike in otel exporter error counter: otel_exporter_otlp_errors_total{exporter="grpc"} increased from ~2/min to 120/min.
- Ingest logs (ingester pod):
  "2024-10-14T22:31:12Z ERROR store-client.go:87 write failed: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = server overloaded"
  "2024-10-14T22:32:01Z WARN queue.go:214 dropped batch id=0x7f52 cause=timeout (enqueue)"
- Example span partial payload seen in proxy logs:
  {"trace_id":"a3f4...","parent_id":"...","name":"model.generate","duration_ms":1450,"status":"OK","attributes":{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"gpt-3.5-small"}}
  followed by:  "otel_exporter: send failed: context deadline exceeded"

Commands I ran (and notes):
- kubectl logs -n observability deploy/obs-ingester --since=45m | grep "ResourceExhausted"\  -> confirmed bursts of ResourceExhausted between 22:30-22:51.
- kubectl exec -n observability -c otel otel-collector-0 -- curl -sS localhost:8888/metrics | grep otel_exporter_otlp\  -> saw exporter errors and long cumulative send durations.
- curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @sample-batch.json http://obs-gateway.internal/v1/logs -v\  -> local replay accepted (200) when gateway under low load; when gateway at >80% CPU it returned 502 or timed out.
- ./scripts/replay.sh sample-batch.json --concurrency 20 --rps 200\  -> reproduced queueing and saw otel exporter timeouts after ~3m.
- kubectl port-forward svc/otel-collector 4317:4317 &\
  python -c "from otlp_sender import send_spans; send_spans('127.0.0.1:4317', 500, batch_size=50)"\  -> isolated OTLP exporter latency spikes mirrored the production pattern (=> likely exporter/backpressure issue).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Backpressure cascade: storage (clickhouse/ES) under pressure returns 429/ResourceExhausted -> ingester queue fills -> exporter timeouts -> metrics drop. Evidence: ResourceExhausted logs + 429s reported.
2) OTLP exporter config bug: timeout too aggressive or TLS handshake failing intermittently. Evidence: "context deadline exceeded" + exporter error counters.
3) Hook registration race: some services start sending traces before ingest hooks are registered, causing early drops. Evidence: traces missing root spans for some requests in the 22:30 window.
4) Compression/content-encoding mismatch: gzipped payloads declared as plain caused partial parsing failures and silent drops in the pipeline. Lower confidence.

Small repro and quick checks to prioritize (do in order):
- A: Reproduce locally with a short replay at scaled RPS that triggers the issue. Use docker-compose variant of obs-ingester with local backend stub that intentionally returns 429 to see queueing. Commands: 
  ./scripts/replay.sh samples/1500-spans.json --concurrency 8 --rps 150 --duration 5m\  watch -n 5 'curl -s localhost:8888/metrics | egrep "logs_ingested_total|otel_exporter_otlp_errors_total|ingester_queue_length"'
- B: Toggle OTEL exporter timeout and retry settings in central collector: increase OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT (env) to 60000ms and set retry policies (max_elapsed_time: 120s). Redeploy collector sidecar and re-run replay.
- C: Quick storage stress test: run a small load test against downstream storage to confirm ResourceExhausted behavior. If downstream returns 429 under moderate load, we need circuit-breaker.
- D: Replay identical payloads with and without Content-Encoding: gzip header to check parser behavior.

Quick config snippets I edited locally (notes):
- collector-config.yaml (templated):
  exporters:
    otlp/grpc:
      endpoint: "storage-cluster.internal:4317"
      tls:
        insecure: false
      timeout: 10s   # change to 60s for experiment
      retry:
        enabled: true
        initial_interval: 5s
        max_interval: 30s
        max_elapsed_time: 120s
- obs-ingester env: INGEST_QUEUE_SIZE=2000 -> default was 500 (we saw queue fills).

Error snippets saved for reference (raw):
- "2024-10-14T22:33:04Z ERROR exporter/grpc: failed to send: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = stream terminated by RST_STREAM"
- "2024-10-14T22:34:30Z WARN uploader: dropped 7 batches due to store timeout (deadline exceeded)"

Observability breadcrumbs (who touched what):
- 22:16 UTC - deploy/obs-ingester scaled from 3->5 (autoscaler).
- 22:25 UTC - central otel-collector config rotated (PR #879 merged at 22:23).
- 22:29 UTC - maintenance window started on storage cluster (DB ops).
- 22:30 UTC - metric drop begins.

Temporary mitigations applied during incident (notes):
- Increased obs-ingester replicas to 8 (reduced immediate 502s but queueing persisted).
- Applied a short-term rate-limit on gateway (rps cap) to keep downstream within limits.
- Rolled back PR #879 (collector config tweak) to test if it altered behaviour; rollback didn't materially change drop (=> less likely root cause).

Next steps / TODO (concrete):
- [ ] Run controlled replay against a fake storage backend that returns 429 with configurable probability. Capture queue length and exporter errors. (Owner: Riley)
- [ ] Add additional exporter-level metrics (queue length, send latency histogram) to central collector. (Owner: Maya)
- [ ] Triage OTLP error traces: correlate exporter error spikes with storage 429s by timestamp. (Owner: Devon)
- [ ] Draft a runbook entry for rapid rate-limiting and circuit-breaker toggles to protect storage. (Owner: SRE runbook)
- [ ] Validate Content-Encoding handling end-to-end for logs and traces. Create a unit test that sends gzipped payload vs uncompressed. (Owner: Eng-Obs)

Notes/brain dump (random):
- If queue_size growth correlates tightly with storage 429s, we should implement an immediate fast-fail path in ingester when backend signals overload (avoid head-of-line blocking).
- Consider adding a token-bucket limiter between gateway and ingester keyed by customer/route to prevent noisy tenants cascading.
- The exporter timeouts appear after queue latency > 2s consistently; this suggests we need better backpressure propagation (grpc flow control tuning?).

Slack/threads to check for context:
- #obs-ingest (thread ts:1698495600.000200) — initial alarms and first mitigation attempts.
- #infra-ops (thread ts:1698499200.000300) — DB team notes about maintenance window.

Files I dropped in this directory for experiments:
- samples/1500-spans.json  (small batch used for replay)
- scripts/replay.sh (thin wrapper that reads env RPS/CONC and posts to gateway)

If I get time: try isolating exporter behavior by replacing exporter with a stub that ACKs immediately or simulates 200ms latency to see system behavior. If stub fixes drop, it's downstream. If not, problem is upstream queue/hook timing.

Final: this is a working scratchpad. Will formalize into incident postmortem once repro is nailed (and owners agree on mitigation).

-- Riley
